subject: Draft MAP & pilot metrics — clarifying economics & true-up mechanics
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@acmecloud.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
Cc: amit.shah@acmecloud.com, jordan.lee@acmecloud.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP & pilot metrics — next steps

Rafael,

Thanks for the draft MAP you shared during the call. Acme is aligned on moving to a two-phase evaluation: a 6-week pilot followed by a capped ramp to production. Before we lock the MAP and hand to procurement, a few open commercial items we need clarified from your side that will affect our internal sign-off: 

- True-up mechanics: if we exceed pilot estimated usage in month 2, how will true-ups be calculated and capped?
- Price protection: we need a guaranteed rate window while we scale so our unit economics aren't
  moving mid-rollout. Can you propose a protection period?
- Definition of billable usage: are embeddings counted differently? Do eval tokens count?
- Milestone acceptance: what does "pilot accepted" formally mean from Redwood's perspective?

Can you reply with a short note and any redline guidance for procurement? Procurement will expect either a markup in the MAP or a companion amendment to the MSA.

Elena
Director, Product Integrations
Acme Cloud

Attachments: Acme_pilot_requirements.xlsx (referenced in call)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmecloud.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & pilot metrics — next steps

Elena — thanks for the concise list. High level responses below; I attached an updated MAP (Redwood_MAP_v2.pdf) that incorporates these items and short options for procurement redlines.

1) True-ups: our standard is to reconcile actual vs committed usage at the end of each calendar quarter during the first 12 months. For pilots we can instead do a 30/60/90-day cadence. We typically propose a true-up for overage = (actual - committed) * list rate, but we are open to a capped approach for the pilot ramp.

2) Price protection: we can provide a fixed unit rate for a defined window starting at first production traffic. For pilots/early ramp we often offer 8-12 weeks of price protection; I think 12 weeks is a reasonable starting place for Acme.

3) Billable usage definition: we bill per-token generation + embedding units. Eval-only test tokens (non-production sandbox) can be scoped out if explicitly segmented. We'll propose a definition in the MAP that distinguishes: (a) dev/eval test traffic, (b) pilot production test traffic, and (c) production traffic.

4) Pilot acceptance: propose two acceptance gates — (A) functional (api responses meet acceptance prompt set) and (B) latency/cost gate (95th pctl latency below agreed SLO and per-token cost within target). If both pass, the pilot moves to ramp.

Next steps: I've looped in Monica (CS) and Ben (AE) to weigh in on the economics and an operational true-up cap we could accept for this MAP. If Acme's procurement wants to redline, please send the document and we'll coordinate legal.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MAP_v2.pdf (MAP + definitions)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Draft MAP & pilot metrics — need pricing/true-up input

Folks — forwarding Acme's note and my reply. Key asks from procurement: price protection window, cap on true-ups during pilot/ramp, and the canonical definition of billable usage. We want to move to a single short amendment that Procurement can sign with minimal redlines.

Specific asks: 
- What cap on retrospective true-ups are we comfortable offering for a pilot? (Ben: propose a percentage cap)
- Recommended price-protection length (Monica: what works for CS operations?)
- Exact wording to exclude eval/sandbox tokens from billables (Karthik: is it safe to ask for a dedicated API key/labeling to guarantee segmentation?)

I would like answers by EOD so I can send an updated MAP to Acme's procurement.

Thanks,
Rafael

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Draft MAP & pilot metrics — need pricing/true-up input

Quick proposal from a commercial perspective — keep it tight and procurement-friendly: 

- Pilot true-up cadence: 30/60/90-day checkpoints. If actual usage exceeds the pilot committed volume during the pilot period, true-ups are limited to the greater of (a) actual overage at list rate, or (b) a 20% cap on the delta versus committed for the pilot period. This prevents runaway retro billing while still protecting Redwood from significant under-commit.

- Production ramp true-up waterfall: months 1-3 post-acceptance: allowed variance +/- 10% without true-up; months 4-6: +/- 5%; after month 6 standard quarterly reconciliation at list rates (no cap).

- Price protection: 12-week fixed rate starting from first production traffic (not pilot start). If we accept, we put a clause that pricing adjustments after the window will be communicated 30 days prior to taking effect.

- Usage definition (recommended clause): "Billable usage shall include inference input and output tokens, embeddings compute units, and any accessory API calls used in the generation path. Development/test traffic identifiable by API key or label provided by Acme and isolated to non-production projects shall be excluded from billable usage."

- Enforcement: require tagging of pilot traffic with an agreed API key; CS (Monica) will help set up monitoring + daily usage feeds so disputes are caught early.

If Acme pushes back on the 20% pilot cap, we can move to a tiered cap: 10% for pilots < $50k, 20% for pilots $50k-$200k, sliding upward.

Happy to own the language and send back a short clause for procurement.

-Ben

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecloud.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
Cc: elena@acmecloud.com, amit.shah@acmecloud.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 14:40:00 -0700
Subject: Acme redlines to MAP and MSA — attached

Rafael — attaching Acme's redlines (Acme_Redlines_20260820.docx). Procurement has a few concerns: 

1) The proposed 20% pilot cap is acceptable only if it applies to inadvertent measurement errors, not to deliberate underreporting. They asked for an audit right but want any retro true-up limited to 10% for the pilot.
2) They want price protection for 6 months post-acceptance, not 12 weeks.
3) They request a narrower definition of billable usage: exclude "evaluation prompts executed using curated prompt sets for benchmarking" even if they use production keys; they propose a separate tracked label for benchmarking.

Procurement attached an annotated DocuSign link they expect a clean MAP + amendment with the redlines incorporated so their procurement counsel can expedite.

-Jordan

Attachment: Acme_Redlines_20260820.docx (redline commentary)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@acmecloud.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecloud.com>, amit.shah@acmecloud.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme redlines to MAP and MSA — path to close

Elena / Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear redlines. Proposed path to close that should be acceptable to both sides and keep procurement moving: 

1) Pilot true-up cap: we can accept a 10% retro true-up cap for the pilot period provided Acme agrees to (a) maintain tagged pilot API keys and (b) allow a one-time audit within 90 days of pilot completion if significant measurement discrepancies are suspected. For deliberate underreporting we reserve standard audit remedies (no cap).

2) Price protection: compromise — 12 weeks by default, with an optional one-time extension to 6 months if Acme commits to a minimum post-acceptance purchase volume (to be defined in the MAP). This gives Redwood protection while enabling Acme to ask for stability in return for a stronger commitment.

3) Billable usage: we'll adopt the language Ben proposed, plus a clearexception for "curated benchmarking prompt sets" that are executed on a labeled benchmarking key and exempt from billables. Procurement must ensure benchmarking keys are distinct and usage is exported to the shared monitoring feed.

4) Milestone acceptance: we will formalize the two gates in the MAP. Pilot acceptance moves to ramp only after both gates pass and signed acceptance email from Acme.

Next steps: Ben will draft the exact clause language for the pilot cap and price-protection extension condition. Monica will confirm labeling + monitoring implementation details. I will circulate an updated MAP and a short amendment incorporating the agreed compromises; timeline: updated docs by Monday, 24 Aug, so procurement can sign early next week. Please confirm if Acme can live with the one-time extension approach for price protection; if not, tell us which specific assurances you need and we will iterate.

Best,
Rafael
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v2.pdf (updated will follow), Proposed_clause_draft.docx (to be sent Monday)
